instruction: Explain what fine-tuning means in one sentence.
output: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained language model to a specific task by training it on a smaller, task-focused dataset.
LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that trains small adapter matrices instead of updating all model weights.
RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) combines document search with text generation so answers are grounded in retrieved context.
An AI agent is a system where an LLM autonomously decides which tools to use in a loop to accomplish a goal.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI applications to connect to external tools and data sources.

input: Embeddings convert text into vectors for semantic search.
output: Embeddings turn text into numerical vectors so similar meanings can be found via vector search.

input: Student asks: Why use LoRA instead of full fine-tuning?
output: LoRA is cheaper and faster because it trains only a small set of adapter weights, making fine-tuning possible on modest hardware.
Prompt engineering is the practice of writing instructions that guide an LLM toward better, more reliable outputs.
A vector database stores text embeddings and finds the most similar items quickly, which powers semantic search in RAG systems.
Tool calling lets an LLM request external functions (like calculators or APIs) by outputting structured tool names and arguments.
Instruction fine-tuning data usually has an instruction, optional input, and the desired output response for the model to learn.
Overfitting happens when the model memorizes training examples instead of learning general patterns, leading to poor performance on new inputs.
A base model is a pre-trained LLM that already knows language patterns and is adapted later for specific tasks via fine-tuning.
Evaluation compares model outputs before and after fine-tuning on held-out examples to verify the model improved on your target task.
Agentic AI systems plan steps, call tools, observe results, and iterate until they complete a task rather than answering in one shot.
